<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 14f4d8f8cd997d3722db0460a0fc7230f793121a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `dc36b9dd62c31f2494215e2c899e0c4eef51df2c` — the merge of head `85f9ed76e6adf42413fb31b51dafb2e745078bd7` into base `14f4d8f8cd997d3722db0460a0fc7230f793121a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin dc36b9dd62c31f2494215e2c899e0c4eef51df2c && git checkout dc36b9dd62c31f2494215e2c899e0c4eef51df2c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 14f4d8f8cd997d3722db0460a0fc7230f793121a 85f9ed76e6adf42413fb31b51dafb2e745078bd7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 14f4d8f8cd997d3722db0460a0fc7230f793121a && git merge --no-ff 85f9ed76e6adf42413fb31b51dafb2e745078bd7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 14f4d8f8cd997d3722db0460a0fc7230f793121a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Head-sha: `bb358a0d6e58e0748ac34e023bf6cb31284b0965`

Scope: packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, skills/objectstack-data/references/examples-objects.md + ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/DetailSection.tsx
Security-touching: no

Inputs read: card #36269 with every comment (ruling 7074368214, claims 7078229847 and 7118735409, release 7080178415, dev report 7119596674), the PR body and its 11-file list, the net diff against merge base `4c93f8807e`, and the check-runs on the head. Nothing was built, run or re-run. The remainder of the diff (five test files, the changeset, `content/docs/data-modeling/schema-design.mdx`, the regenerated `content/docs/references/data/object.mdx`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT and is not reviewed here.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set of `ObjectFieldGroupSchema`: unchanged. The `collapse` enum, its `.optional().default('none')` and the strict-key refusal list are the same; the diff edits one refusal message string, one TSDoc block and one `.describe()`. Right, and it agrees with the claim's `Clause-②: no`.
- Public types and exports of `@objectstack/spec` and `@object-ui/plugin-detail`: unchanged. `DetailSection` keeps its props; the synth (`buildDefaultPageSchema.ts`) is not in the diff and still emits `collapsible` only for a non-`'none'` group and `defaultCollapsed` only for `'collapsed'`. Right.
- Published text: the `collapse` describe gains one sentence, and `content/docs/references/data/object.mdx` carries the same sentence in all five tables that render it. Right; `check:generated` is inside the green `Lint & Repo Gates` family.
- Behaviour: on the frameless face (drawn only under `DefaultRecordPageContext` and never on a print page) a titled section with no `collapsible` changes from a plain `h3` to the title-row button with `aria-expanded`. This is the semantic change the ruling orders (item 1) and it is declared as `Metadata-protocol: semantic`. Right.
- Gate verdicts on the head: every check-run concluded `success` or `skipped`; none failed. `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Test UI` (16 shards), `Test Core` (10 shards), `Type Check UI`, `Build & E2E UI` and `Live E2E UI` are green.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/36269-every-group-folds.md` grades `@objectstack/spec` minor and `@object-ui/plugin-detail` minor and carries `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: semantic`; the PR body carries the same two lines. The meaning of an authorable key changes on one surface, which AGENTS.md grades `semantic` and at least `minor` on a package the diff moves. Both packages have published source in the diff. The level matches what the diff publishes.

Clause-②: no. No accepted key, value, default or exported type changes.

No ADR-0087 entry is in the diff. No stored metadata needs rewriting (no key or value is renamed, refused or re-defaulted), and no gate on the head asked for one.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev `open_questions` 1 (the `skills/**` hunk on an `area:ux` PR): answered, option A. Ruling 7074368214 names "any skill text that teaches `'none'` as no toggle on every surface" as part of this change, and the PR is Tier H by the same ruling. The hunk stays.
- ADR-0085 addendum: escalated to the seat. The ruling says "the build carries an ADR-0085 addendum" and lists it under "Wording in the same change". This PR carries none, and cites claim 7078229847 ("a separate domain:skills card, asked of the seat 08:24Z"). I searched the tracker and found no such card, which does not prove there is none. After this lands, ADR-0085 §4 and §5 on `main` still read as one meaning on every surface while the spec describe says otherwise. The seat names the addendum card on this PR before it lands, or files it.
- The titled ungrouped bucket: answered, within the ruling. On the running app `deriveRecordDetailSections` (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/recordDetailSections.ts`, outside the diff) gives the ungrouped bucket of a grouped object the `common.ungroupedSection` heading, so that bucket is titled and now folds (the PR's own acceptance line shows `Other=open` with a toggle). The ruling's "the untitled ungrouped bucket has no toggle" therefore holds only for a section drawn with no title, which is what the tests pin. The ruling's reader-facing sentence is "every titled group", so this matches it; the maintainer should know the "Other" group folds too.
- `content/docs/data-modeling/schema-design.mdx` line 332 still says "Groups render identically on forms, modals, and detail pages", twelve lines below the `collapse` row this PR rewrites, and it is the same sentence this PR removes from the skill. That file is the lane seat's remainder, so the sentence is not graded here; it is handed to the lane seat.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.
- Security: no changed hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour. The skill hunk changes the `collapse` bullet only; the neighbouring `requiresFeature` bullet is untouched.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`** (against ruling 7074368214 and its first consumer, `DetailSection.tsx`)

- The `.describe()` sentence holds: on the head's frameless face a titled section folds whatever `collapsible` says, and the first state is `defaultCollapsed`, which the synth sets for `'collapsed'` alone. `'none'` and `'expanded'` start open.
- The TSDoc holds for forms and the designer preview (ruling item 3; no form file is in the diff).
- The refusal message for a stray `expanded` key holds.
- S1 (should-fix) — `packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts` line 123, the published object form in the same package, still gives the `collapse` setting the help text "Whether the section can be collapsed, on the entry form and the record detail page. Unset: none." with the option "None — always open, no toggle". After this change that sentence is false for the default record page. The ruling's facet ③ names exactly this as the one trap the wording change has to state (an author choosing `'none'` to remove the arrow on the record page), and this form is where a human author makes that choice. The same string is generated into `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/en.metadata-forms.generated.ts`. The fix is one help-text sentence plus its regenerated copies, in this PR or in a follow-up card the seat names here; the claim's file surface lists the `collapse` describe only, so the seat decides which.
- N1 (nit) — the TSDoc names forms and the designer preview as the surfaces that follow the three states as written. An authored record page and a print page also do not take the reader-fold rule (the card face still reads `collapsible`; print draws open). The sentence is not wrong, only incomplete.

**`skills/objectstack-data/references/examples-objects.md`** (against the spec it teaches and the ruling's facet ③)

- The removed sentence, "Groups render identically on forms, modals, and detail pages", was the text the ruling orders changed. The new sentence, "the default record page lets readers fold any titled group", is true on the head and states the trap. `'collapsed' starts closed` is true on every surface. No other file under `skills/` teaches `'none'` as "no toggle" (searched at the head).
- N2 (nit) — "Forms keep it" is terse; "it" is the `collapse` value as written. The meaning is recoverable from the bullet, and the file sits under the token ratchet.

**`ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/DetailSection.tsx`** (implementing file, against the contract sentence by sentence)

- "Every titled group folds": the two `section.title` branches are merged into one button, with `aria-expanded`, the chevron at the row's right end and the whole row as the click target. Holds.
- "`collapse` picks the first state": `React.useState(section.defaultCollapsed ?? false)` is unchanged. Holds.
- "The untitled bucket has no toggle": the button is behind `section.title`. Holds.
- "Print draws open; forms, designer preview and authored pages unchanged": `frameless = useDefaultRecordPage() && !isPrintPage`; the card and disclosure faces below still read `section.collapsible`. `RecordDetailView.tsx` provides the context as `!assignedPage && !namedPageBlocked`. Holds.
- "System information stays closed": `RecordMetaFooter.tsx` is not in the diff and still passes `collapsible: true, defaultCollapsed: true`. Holds.
- The reported body rows (`drawsContent`, line 580) already treated a closed frameless section as drawing nothing, so the owner line stays correct when a `'none'` group is folded. Holds.
- Tried to break it: a section with `defaultCollapsed: true` and no `collapsible` was already drawn closed on this face before the change, with no way to open it; it now has a toggle, which is an improvement.
- N3 (nit) — for that same shape, `sectionDrawnClosed` in `synth/buildDefaultPageSchema.ts` (outside the diff, read only) still requires `collapsible === true && defaultCollapsed === true`, so it counts as open a section the face draws closed. Group references are unaffected, because the synth never sets one without the other. This predates the PR; a follow-up card if the seat wants the two readers aligned.

No must-fix. One should-fix (S1) is open on this head and earns a delta review of its fix.

- **M1 (claim surface, paper).** Claim 7118735409's file surface is `ui/packages/plugin-detail/**`, the `object.zod.ts` describe plus its regenerated reference, and `content/docs/**/schema-design.mdx`. The diff also edits `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.accessibleNames-12625.test.tsx`, an existing test outside that surface. The pin that asserted `getByRole('heading', { name: 'Address' })` (`recordPageV3Face-27055.test.tsx`) was replaced, not kept beside the new button assertion. That is the form where an author picks `'none'`: the ruling's facet ③ trap. I checked the line at this head. The seat decides whether it is fixed in this PR (claim amendment) or in a follow-up card named here. Under the nit-only merge standard it is fixed and delta-read before landing either way, unless the seat moves it to a named card.
- **Seat item (ruling compliance, not graded here).** Ruling 7074368214 lists an ADR-0085 addendum under "Wording in the same change". The PR defers it to "a separate card (claim 7078229847)", and no such card number is cited anywhere. The L2 search found none. Before the hand-off to the approver, the seat names the addendum card on this PR or files it.

- **N1 (from L2).** The `object.zod.ts` TSDoc names forms and the designer preview as following the three states as written; authored record pages and print also do. Incomplete, not wrong.

- **N4.** The titled "Other" (ungrouped) bucket folds too, because `recordDetailSections.ts` titles it. This is within the ruling's "every titled group" but worth one line to the approver.

Delta read owed on the next head: S1, S2, and whichever way the L2 S1 goes. M1 is closed by the claim amendment and the body line.
